Subject: ACME - Post-call TCO recap & next steps

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and the cost/TCO levers we discussed so your team has something to share internally. Let me know if I missed anything.

Pain points you shared:
- High inference spend driven by bursty customer traffic and large context windows (~1.2k tokens per request on average).
- Unpredictable monthly spend due to lack of batching and no prefix/KV caching in the current pipeline.
- Need for predictable pricing to get internal approval; current invoices spike during launches.

Goals / success criteria:
- Bring average per-request cost down by 40% while keeping p95 latency < 300ms for user-facing flows.
- Pilot at ~50M tokens/month with clear cost estimate and instrumentation to measure user-level ROI.
- Narrow list of acceptable models and quantization profiles for initial pilot.

Cost / TCO levers we recommend (short version):
1) Token economics: we modeled per-token unit costs assuming 8-bit quantized variants for your LLM family. Small changes in average context length and prompt engineering could reduce token consumption by ~15-25%.
2) Batching: enable small-request batching for background jobs and medium batching for non-interactive flows — expected 20-35% unit cost reduction without impacting interactive latency targets when combined with dynamic routing.
3) KV/prefix caching: for repeated prompts (e.g., customer histories), caching reduces generation tokens and model compute — 10-30% savings depending on cache hit rate.
4) Model/quantization mix: using a mixed fleet (higher-cap for low-latency endpoints, more-quantized cheap variants for background tasks) gives predictable SLAs at lower blended cost.

What we need from you to finalize a tailored pilot estimate: 
- Current monthly token usage (approx).
- Typical distribution: interactive vs. background job tokens (or % of requests with long context).
- Peak qps and acceptable p95 latency target for interactive flows.

Next steps / proposal:
- I attached a short TCO workbook (redwood_tco_workbook.xlsx) with an initial model showing savings across levers.
- If you can share monthly token snapshot (or the ad-hoc CSV), Rafael and I will produce a 1-page pilot estimate and a recommended config.
- Proposed follow-up: 60-min call week of Jun 22 to align pilot scope and success metrics.

Appreciate you looping Bob in here if he’s the right owner for budget/finance.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
